outcome: As of the search (11 Oct 2026) the Elliott–Halberstam conjecture itself, for every level θ < 1, is still unproved and no source claims a deterministic proof; since 26 Jan 2024 the record holds conditional results (EH under GRH plus a pair-correlation conjecture), unconditional progress on weighted or smooth-modulus variants (distribution level 5/8 for weighted sums, 10/19 for a minorant on smooth moduli), and a 2026 race on bounded prime gaps (H1 ≤ 240, 236, 212, 186) that concerns a different quantity.
problem_asks: The bullet names one conjecture and states no quantity, so the content it refers to is written out here from the standard formulation; the 1968 wording is not reproduced in the Wikipedia article, which says it must be inferred from the 1968 paper. Parts: (1) for every θ with 0 < θ < 1 (Wikipedia: 'for every θ < 1'), the primes have level of distribution θ; (2) for every A > 0; (3) Σ over moduli q ≤ x^θ of E*(x,q) ≪ x/(log x)^A, where E*(x,q) is the largest deviation max over y ≤ x and over residue classes a coprime to q of |ψ(y;q,a) − y/φ(q)|, the implied constant depending only on θ and A. The bullet does not ask for a restricted range, weighted sums, smooth moduli, or the consequences for prime gaps or twin primes. The θ = 1 endpoint is known to fail in the log-power form (Friedlander–Granville 1989), so the conjecture is for θ < 1.

events.what_happened: Bombieri and Vinogradov proved the averaged distribution of primes in arithmetic progressions for moduli up to x^θ with θ < 1/2 (the Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem). The Wikipedia EH article cites Bombieri, 'On the large sieve', Mathematika 12 (1965), and Vinogradov's paper on the density hypothesis (Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR, 1965). The primary papers were not opened; this rests on the Wikipedia article. Classical result; this record did not search for post-publication reviews.
events.delivers: The unweighted EH-type sum with the maximum over y ≤ x, for every θ < 1/2, all moduli. Settles the range θ < 1/2 only.
events.remains: Every θ in [1/2, 1); the conjecture's full range θ < 1.
events.direction: Agrees with the conjectured bound, but only in the range θ < 1/2, which is the unconditional baseline the conjecture improves on.

events.what_happened: Friedlander and Granville, 'Limitations to the equi-distribution of primes I', Annals of Mathematics 129 (1989), 363–382. For any fixed N > 0 there are arbitrarily large a and x for which the sum over moduli q < x/(log x)^N, (q,a)=1, of |ψ(x;q,a) − x/φ(q)| is at least a constant times x. The abstract states that this disproves conjectures of Elliott and Halberstam and of Montgomery. Building on Maier's method. The Annals abstract was opened; the Wikipedia EH article says the conjecture is known to fail at the endpoint θ = 1.
events.revisions: Publication DOI 10.2307/1971450; the journal page gives only the year. The first public version may predate the journal.
events.delivers: Refutes the endpoint form of the sum at level 1 once the moduli extend to x/(log x)^N. The counterexample uses q beyond x^(1-ε), so it does not reach the conjecture's stated range θ < 1 as written.
events.remains: The conjecture for every θ < 1 is not touched by this counterexample. Whether power-range versions hold for θ < 1 is open in the sources read.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper, vol. 129, issue 2 (1989)

events.direction: Cuts against the conjecture only at the endpoint: the sum over moduli up to x/(log x)^N fails, so the conjecture cannot be stated at level 1 without a power saving. Consistent with the conjecture for θ < 1 as stated on Wikipedia. A later Friedlander–Granville–Hildebrand–Maier counterexample at a somewhat larger range is cited by a 2023 arXiv paper (arXiv 2311.09464, not opened).
events.object: Existence statement: arbitrarily large a and x for which the sum is ≫ x. Non-constructive in the abstract; no explicit a, x given.

events.what_happened: D.H.J. Polymath, 'New equidistribution estimates of Zhang type', arXiv 1402.0811 (first submitted 4 Feb 2014, revised to v3 on 3 Sep 2014), Algebra & Number Theory 8 (2014) 2067–2199. Proves distribution of primes in arithmetic progressions to large smooth squarefree moduli, for congruence classes satisfying CRT conditions, with exponent 1/2 + 7/300.
events.revisions: v1 4 Feb 2014; v3 3 Sep 2014; journal Algebra & Number Theory 8 (2014).
events.delivers: A level of distribution 1/2 + 7/300 for a restricted class: large smooth squarefree moduli, with CRT-type congruence classes. Not the unweighted sum over all moduli.
events.remains: All moduli, i.e. the full sum over q ≤ x^θ for any θ in (1/2, 1); the full EH conjecture.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper, vol. 8 (2014), pp. 2067–2199

events.direction: Moves the level above 1/2 for a restricted class of moduli. Not a move in the unrestricted quantity the conjecture asks about.

events.what_happened: James Maynard, 'Small gaps between primes', arXiv 1311.4600 (first submitted 19 Nov 2013). Proves liminf (p_{n+1} − p_n) ≤ 600 unconditionally, and states that if the Elliott–Halberstam conjecture is assumed, liminf (p_{n+1} − p_n) ≤ 12 and liminf (p_{n+2} − p_n) ≤ 600. The arXiv page was opened; the journal (Annals of Mathematics 181, 2015) was not opened.
events.revisions: v1 19 Nov 2013; later published in Annals of Mathematics 181 (2015) (journal listing seen in a search result, not opened).
events.delivers: Conditional on EH: a gap bound 12. Unconditionally: 600. The EH hypothesis is used as an assumption; the paper does not prove EH.
events.remains: EH itself.
events.direction: Conditional consequence of EH. Does not bear on whether EH holds. Recorded because it is the main conditional use of the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Terence Tao, 'The Elliott-Halberstam conjecture implies the Vinogradov least quadratic nonresidue conjecture', arXiv 1410.7073 (first submitted 26 Oct 2014; v3 13 Jan 2015), Algebra & Number Theory 9 (2015) 1005–1034. Shows Vinogradov's conjecture follows from EH.
events.revisions: v1 26 Oct 2014; v2 29 Oct 2014; v3 13 Jan 2015; journal Algebra & Number Theory 9 (2015).
events.delivers: Conditional on EH (for θ in the conjectured range): Vinogradov's least quadratic non-residue conjecture. Does not prove EH.
events.remains: EH itself.
events.direction: Conditional consequence of EH. Does not bear on whether EH holds.

events.what_happened: Victor Volfson, 'Probabilistic approach to the distribution of primes and to the proof of Legendre and Elliott-Halberstam conjectures', arXiv 1501.07267 (first submitted 28 Jan 2015; v2 1 Mar 2015; comments '23 pages'; no journal reference). The abstract claims that the Elliott–Halberstam conjecture 'was proved in this paper with probability arbitrarily close to 1 for all 0<a<1 and A>0', via probabilistic estimates for the error terms that the author says are stronger than GRH-based ones. The arXiv abstract page was opened; the paper body was not.
events.revisions: v1 28 Jan 2015; v2 1 Mar 2015 (current).
events.delivers: As claimed: a probabilistic version of the EH bound, holding with probability arbitrarily close to 1. Not the deterministic statement that the conjecture asserts for every x and q.
events.remains: The deterministic conjecture for every θ < 1, as far as the abstract shows.
events.doubts: The conjecture asserts a bound for all x and all moduli; the claim is a bound holding with probability close to 1, so it does not obviously give the deterministic statement. The abstract gives no reason why the probabilistic version implies the deterministic one. No journal reference, no withdrawal notice, and no reviews were found in searches; this is weak evidence of no engagement, since the searches were not exhaustive.
events.direction: Claims EH in a probabilistic form. Whether that is the conjecture is the judging pass's call; the abstract's own wording is 'with probability arbitrarily close to 1'.

events.what_happened: Nathalie Debouzy, 'Twins almost prime under a Elliott-Halberstam's conjecture', arXiv 1907.06393 (15 Jul 2019, single version, no journal reference). Under an EH-type conjecture, proves there are infinitely many twins almost primes. The arXiv abstract was opened; the paper body was not. Engagement was not searched for specifically.
events.revisions: v1 only, 15 Jul 2019.
events.delivers: Conditional on an EH-type hypothesis: infinitely many twins almost primes. Does not prove EH.
events.remains: EH itself.
events.direction: Conditional consequence of EH. Does not bear on whether EH holds.

events.what_happened: Jared Duker Lichtman, 'Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli, and Goldbach beyond the square-root barrier', arXiv 2309.08522 (v1 30 Aug 2023; appendix with Sary Drappeau; no journal listed). Abstract: the primes have level of distribution 66/107 ≈ 0.617 using triply well-factorable weights; extended to 5/8 assuming Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture. The arXiv abstract was opened; the main theorem was not readable from the abstract page.
events.revisions: Single version v1 (30 Aug 2023) as listed.
events.delivers: A level 66/107 for weighted sums with triply well-factorable weights; a level 5/8 conditional on Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture. Whether the unweighted sum over all moduli is covered is not established in the abstract read.
events.remains: The unweighted sum over all moduli for any θ > 1/2; the unconditional 5/8 level for unweighted sums; EH.
events.doubts: The 5/8 level is conditional on Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture. A 2026 arXiv paper (not opened, seen in a search result) attributes 153/256 to Lichtman's Theorem 1.7; that conflicts with the 66/107 abstract figure.
events.direction: Moves the weighted level above the conjectured-type 1/2 barrier. The weights make this a different sum from the unweighted EH quantity; the judging pass must decide whether it moves the quantity the conjecture names.

events.what_happened: Julia Stadlmann, 'On primes in arithmetic progressions and bounded gaps between many primes', arXiv 2309.00425 (v1 1 Sep 2023; v2 11 Oct 2023; v3 22 Feb 2025). Proves the primes below x are on average equidistributed in arithmetic progressions to smooth moduli up to x^(1/2+1/40−ε), improving Polymath's 1/2 + 7/300. The comments field says accepted for Advances in Mathematics (the volume 468 (2025) was seen in a search result, not opened).
events.revisions: v1 1 Sep 2023; v2 11 Oct 2023; v3 22 Feb 2025 (current).
events.delivers: A level 1/2 + 1/40 for smooth moduli only. Not the full sum over all moduli.
events.remains: Non-smooth moduli; levels above 1/2 + 1/40 for smooth moduli; EH.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted per arXiv comments; volume 468 (2025) seen in a search result, not verified

events.direction: Moves the level above 1/2 for smooth moduli only. A restricted class, not the unrestricted EH quantity.

events.what_happened: Alexandru Pascadi, 'Large sieve inequalities for exceptional Maass forms and the greatest prime factor of n^2+1', arXiv 2404.04239 (v1 5 Apr 2024; v2 8 Jan 2025; v3 15 Jan 2026). The abstract announces 'applications to the exponents of distribution of primes and smooth numbers in arithmetic progressions'. The abstract was opened. The mathematics for the prime application is not in this version; it appears in the split paper arXiv 2505.00653 (May 2025) per that paper's comments.
events.delivers: Nothing on EH in the abstract: an announcement that applications to the exponents of distribution exist. No level is stated in the abstract read.
events.remains: All of EH.
events.doubts: The EH-type claim is announced in the abstract, not argued in this version; the argument is in arXiv 2505.00653.
events.direction: No direction on EH in this version; announces the application recorded in the next event.

events.what_happened: Neelam Kandhil, Alessandro Languasco, Pieter Moree, 'Pair Correlation of zeros of Dirichlet L-Functions: A possible path towards the conjectures of Chowla, Elliott-Halberstam and Montgomery', arXiv 2411.19762 (v1 29 Nov 2024; v2 8 Nov 2025). Assuming GRH and a pair-correlation conjecture for zeros of Dirichlet L-functions, proves Montgomery's conjecture (in the Friedlander–Granville corrected form) and states that 'under the same assumptions, the Elliott-Halberstam conjecture holds true'. Journal reference: Math. Ann. 394, 43 (2026), DOI 10.1007/s00208-026-03383-y.
events.revisions: v1 29 Nov 2024; v2 8 Nov 2025; published Math. Ann. 394 (2026) per the arXiv journal reference.
events.delivers: EH holds, but only under GRH plus a pair-correlation conjecture for Dirichlet L-functions. A conditional version of the conjecture; the abstract states the result under those hypotheses.
events.remains: EH unconditionally, for every θ < 1, is open on the record read.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published, Math. Ann. 394, 43 (2026), per the arXiv journal reference

events.doubts: The result depends on two hypotheses that are unproven (GRH, and a pair-correlation conjecture). It is a different-hypotheses version of EH, so it does not settle the unconditional conjecture.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture: EH holds under extra hypotheses. The hypotheses are the part that makes it a different question.

events.what_happened: Milad Ghadimi, 'Heuristic Bounded Prime Gaps via a Chaotic Multidimensional Sieve and Random Matrix Theory', arXiv 2507.17986 (23 Jul 2025, single version). Heuristically suggests unconditional prime gaps of at most 180 and, under a partial Elliott–Halberstam conjecture with δ = 0.3, gaps of at most 8. The abstract says the author distinguishes heuristic from conjectural arguments and gives rigorous proofs only for certain analytic components. The arXiv abstract was opened.
events.revisions: Single version v1, 23 Jul 2025.
events.delivers: Heuristic gap bounds; conditional on a partial EH hypothesis with δ = 0.3. Does not establish any level of distribution.
events.remains: EH; the unconditional and partial-EH hypotheses are assumed, not proved.
events.doubts: The author describes the central numbers as heuristic and supported by numerics up to 10^18, not proved. No journal, review, or expert comment was found.
events.direction: Heuristic only; does not move the level of distribution.

events.what_happened: Runbo Li, 'Primes in arithmetic progressions to smooth moduli: A minorant version', arXiv 2505.09629 (v1 30 Apr 2025; v2 17 Oct 2025; v3 29 Dec 2025, comments say 'Corrected an error in the proof'). Abstract: a function ρ(n) minorises the prime indicator function and has distribution level 10/19 in arithmetic progressions to smooth moduli; refines Baker–Irving and Stadlmann. The arXiv abstract page was opened; the body was not.
events.revisions: v1 30 Apr 2025; v2 17 Oct 2025; v3 29 Dec 2025 (correction to the proof).
events.delivers: A minorant for the prime indicator with level 10/19 on smooth moduli. Not the sum of prime error terms over all moduli, and the object is a minorant, not the primes themselves.
events.remains: Non-smooth moduli; the unrestricted prime sum; EH.
events.doubts: v3 says an error in the proof was corrected in December 2025; the body was not read to check the correction. A ResearchGate listing of the same title (not opened) gives 65/123 rather than 10/19, which is unresolved.
events.direction: Moves the level above 1/2 for smooth moduli, through a minorant rather than the primes. A restricted, modified object.
events.object: A function ρ(n) minorising the prime indicator, with distribution level 10/19 on smooth moduli. The abstract does not describe its form.

events.what_happened: Alexandru Pascadi, 'On the exponents of distribution of primes and smooth numbers', arXiv 2505.00653 (v1 1 May 2025; v2 29 Jun 2025, typo corrections; split from arXiv 2404.04239). Abstract: primes and smooth numbers are equidistributed in arithmetic progressions to moduli up to x^(5/8−o(1)); uses triply well-factorable weights for primes; removes the dependence on Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture present in earlier work; applications to twin primes and consecutive smooth numbers. The arXiv abstract page was opened; the body was not.
events.revisions: v1 1 May 2025; v2 29 Jun 2025 (typo corrections). No journal reference listed.
events.delivers: A level 5/8 − o(1) for primes in arithmetic progressions, for weighted sums with triply well-factorable weights, with no dependence on Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture according to the abstract. It is a weighted statement, not the unweighted sum over q ≤ x^θ; whether the moduli are restricted is not stated in the abstract.
events.remains: The unweighted sum over all moduli for any θ > 1/2; the unweighted EH conjecture for θ up to 1.
events.doubts: Weighted level, not unweighted. Whether the 5/8 is stated for all moduli or a restricted class was not readable from the abstract. The abstract states the removal of Selberg-eigenvalue dependence, which is the point a reader would verify in the body. No journal listed; no review found.
events.direction: Moves the best known weighted level for primes in arithmetic progressions above 66/107 (the abstract's own comparison is to the earlier record of Lichtman, per the Lichtman entry), and makes it unconditional. Whether this counts as moving the quantity the conjecture names is the judging pass's call: the weights differ from the unweighted sum.

events.what_happened: Trey Smith, 'A Generalized Elliott-Halberstam Conjecture Implying the Twin Prime Hypothesis', arXiv 2511.14810 (17 Nov 2025, single author, 5 pages, math.NT). Proposes GEH-2, a generalisation of EH for shifted convolutions of the von Mangoldt function, and states 'We show that GEH-2 implies the twin prime conjecture'. The arXiv abstract page was opened.
events.revisions: Only v1 listed.
events.delivers: A conditional implication: GEH-2 implies the twin prime conjecture. GEH-2 is a different hypothesis (shifted correlations of the von Mangoldt function) and is not EH as stated; the paper proposes it rather than proving it.
events.remains: EH; GEH-2 itself is unproved.
events.doubts: A single-author proposal of a new conjecture, with no referee or expert engagement found. The implication is stated; the abstract read does not show the argument.
events.direction: Cuts toward a related conjecture for prime pairs, not EH. The conditional claim concerns twin primes.

events.what_happened: Zongkun Zheng, 'Primes in simultaneous arithmetic progressions', arXiv 2512.22798 (28 Dec 2025, one version, 49 pages). A mean-value theorem for primes lying in two simultaneous arithmetic progressions, built on Bombieri–Fouvry–Friedlander–Iwaniec methods; application: for infinitely many Chen primes p, the greatest prime factor of p+6 exceeds p^0.217. The arXiv abstract page was opened.
events.revisions: Single version v1.
events.delivers: A mean-value estimate for primes in two simultaneous progressions. Not a level of distribution for single progressions, per the abstract.
events.remains: The single-progression EH sum; EH.
events.direction: Different question (two simultaneous congruence conditions). Recorded because it is in the same area.

events.what_happened: Marco Cantarini, 'Averages of diagonal Elliott-Halberstam problem twisted by Möbius function with Sobolev and Hölder-Zygmund weights', arXiv 2607.09110 (10 Jul 2026, math.NT). Under GRH and a weak Gonek–Hejhal conjecture, shows weighted averages of the Möbius-twisted diagonal EH problem match the diagonal bound for W^{2,1} weights over 0<θ<1, and for Hölder–Zygmund weights only for θ depending on δ. The abstract notes that the twisted conjecture together with classical EH would prove binary Goldbach. The arXiv abstract was opened (summarised by the fetch tool; full verbatim text not returned).
events.revisions: Only v1 listed.
events.delivers: Conditional on GRH and a weak Gonek–Hejhal conjecture: weighted versions of a Möbius-twisted EH average. Does not prove classical EH or the twisted conjecture.
events.remains: Classical EH; the twisted conjecture; unconditional weighted versions.
events.doubts: Conditional on GRH and a weak Gonek–Hejhal conjecture; a different (twisted, weighted) question.
events.direction: A conditional result on a twisted variant. Settles nothing for classical EH.

events.what_happened: Neelam Kandhil, Alessandro Languasco, Pieter Moree, 'Beyond the Riemann Hypothesis bounds: A pair-correlation approach to the least prime in arithmetic progression and the smallest quadratic non-residue', arXiv 2607.14515 (16 Jul 2026, one version). Under GRH and specific pair-correlation hypotheses, gives sharper bounds for the least prime in an arithmetic progression and the least quadratic non-residue. The arXiv abstract was opened. A search snippet (not opened) says the paper assumes EH to improve the least-prime bound to p(k) < k^(1+ε) for almost all k; the abstract read does not mention EH.
events.revisions: Only v1 listed.
events.delivers: Conditional on GRH plus pair-correlation hypotheses: sharper least-prime bounds. The EH mention, if any, is conditional and unverified here.
events.remains: EH; unconditional least-prime bounds.
events.doubts: The abstract read says the results are conditional on GRH and specific pair-correlation hypotheses. The EH conditional statement appears only in a search snippet, which conflicts with the abstract read.
events.direction: Conditional, and about a different quantity (least prime). Settles nothing for EH.

events.what_happened: A GitHub issue in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures, #3687, titled 'Elliott–Halberstam conjecture', opened 2 Apr 2026 by a user 'franzhusch' and stating the conjecture as 'for every 0 < ϑ < 1 and every A > 0' with the bound sum over q ≤ x^ϑ of max over y ≤ x of |E(y;q)| ≪ x/(log x)^A. The issue text says it 'was generated by an AI agent and reviewed by' the author; the agent is not named. Closed as completed 20 Jul 2026 via PR #4459 (commit 'feat(Wikipedia): add Elliott–Halberstam conjecture'). The issue page was opened; PR #4459 was not.
events.revisions: Closed as completed 2026-07-20 via PR #4459 (not opened).
events.delivers: A written statement of the conjecture for every 0 < ϑ < 1. It is a statement, not a proof, and the issue says it 'may contain subtle errors'. The issue lists a 2/5 formalizability rating and the missing building blocks.
events.remains: Everything: the statement is not a result.
events.doubts: The issue says the statement 'may contain subtle errors'. Whether the committed Lean file is sorry-free was not established. Only one comment on the issue.
events.direction: No direction on truth; a formal statement of EH for every 0 < ϑ < 1.

events.what_happened: Julia Stadlmann, 'Bounded gaps between primes', arXiv 2608.31126 (v1 31 Aug 2026, math.NT). Combines Bombieri–Vinogradov with newer equidistribution estimates for smooth moduli to obtain H1 ≤ 240 (previous record 246, Polymath8b). Section 1 says Zhang-type estimates exceed exponent 1/2 but apply only to x^δ-smooth moduli, and that the new estimates handle moduli with a large x^δ-smooth factor. No numerical level for the new estimates appears in the part read (first 100,000 characters). The arXiv abstract and HTML were opened.
events.revisions: Only v1 listed.
events.delivers: A bound on H1 (bounded gaps), not on the level of distribution. Uses equidistribution estimates for smooth-factor moduli, which the paper does not state numerically in the part read.
events.remains: EH; any unconditional level above 1/2 for all moduli.
events.doubts: A preprint with no journal listed. Thomas Bloom publicly praised the result on X (seen in a search result; the post was not opened). No verification of the argument by a named expert was found.
events.direction: Lowers the H1 bound. A different quantity from EH; the equidistribution inputs are restricted-modulus estimates.

events.what_happened: OpenAI repository openai/PrimeGaps186, 'Conditional Lean formalization and numerical certificate for prime gaps at most 186', and an OpenAI paper 'Improved short gaps between primes' (PDF, not readable here; the Wikipedia AI-discoveries list dates it 30 Aug 2026; press reports say it accompanied a 3 Sep 2026 model release). The repository gives a Lean 4 derivation of DHL[40,2] from three axioms (rank-three hyper-Kloosterman bound; rank-two Kloosterman correlation bound 8p√p; physical integral and cap bounds), and applies it to an admissible tuple of diameter 186 to get liminf of prime gaps ≤ 186. The README says the axioms 'remain conditional' and that the cited estimates and numerics 'have not been turned into Lean proofs of those inputs'. The repository's formalization.yaml names the model 'GPT 6 Astra' and the framework 'Codex'. Per a search summary of the PDF (not read), the method uses equidistribution estimates from Polymath8a and Stadlmann with factorisation conditions making moduli triply densely divisible.
events.revisions: Date conflicts: 30 Aug 2026 (Wikipedia AI list, PDF date per search summary); 2 Sep 2026 (registry URL); 3 Sep 2026 (press). The repository page footer shows only '© 2026'.
events.delivers: Liminf of prime gaps ≤ 186, conditional on the three axioms; the Lean development establishes only the implication from them. The three axioms are Kloosterman-sum and integral bounds, not EH. The README does not mention EH or a level of distribution.
events.remains: Unconditional H1 ≤ 186; EH; the three axioms themselves.

machine_checked.system: Lean 4 with Mathlib (version as stated in the repository is not confirmed in the read text)

events.directly_checkable: The numerical certificate is a Python script (prime_gap_186_certificate.py) that recomputes the trial; not run here.
events.doubts: Conditional on three axioms, not proved. The formalization.yaml says 'No independent human semantic review.' The registry notes no outside check. The factorisation-conditions step credited to GPT-6 in a public post by an OpenAI-affiliated researcher (X, not opened) is not in any opened primary source. The VibeMathed correction of 22 Sep 2026 says 'Lean-checked, statement unaudited' (secondhand).
events.direction: Cuts toward a bounded-gap bound (H1 ≤ 186), conditional on analytic inputs; not about EH.
events.object: An admissible tuple (40 shifts) of diameter 186; the Lean development applies DHL[40,2] to it, using the three axioms. Explicit tuple; the README says the tuple is included in the repository.
people: OpenAI (organisation; no individual author named in the README)
Weijie Su (OpenAI-affiliated researcher; X post, not opened)

systems.name: GPT 6 Astra
systems.what_it_did: Per the repository metadata: automation method 'agent', framework 'Codex', and the Lean formalisation of the conditional development. The formalization.yaml says the project was 'Refined through human-guided edits and automated proof checks'. A public post by Weijie Su (X, not opened) says the model found complementary factorisation conditions for triply densely divisible moduli; that claim is secondhand and unverified here.
systems.basis_quote: Refined through human-guided edits and automated proof checks.

events.what_happened: Axiom Math announced on 3 Sep 2026 that infinitely many prime pairs are separated by at most 212 (H1 ≤ 212), with a Lean certificate of the deduction of Theorem 1.1 produced by AxiomProver. The paper (primegaps.axiommath.ai/bgp212.pdf) and Axiom's X post were not readable here (the PDF returned binary). The description rests on the whataifound registry entry (opened), VibeMathed, and search summaries, which quote Appendix A of the paper as saying AxiomProver 'autonomously generated from natural-language specifications a Lean certificate of the deduction of Theorem 1.1', and say the certificate is conditional on the equidistribution estimates and the Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem stated in the paper. The registry names nine credited humans.
events.revisions: A final arXiv version was said to follow with the Lean formalisation; not found.
events.delivers: Bounded gaps H1 ≤ 212, as a deduction from the stated analytic inputs (equidistribution estimates and Bombieri–Vinogradov, per the secondhand description). Not EH.
events.remains: EH; the analytic inputs are taken as given.

machine_checked.system: Lean (per the registry; version not stated)

events.doubts: Only company and third-party posts. The registry says no one outside the lab has checked it and the Lean build was not reproduced. Analytic inputs are conditional. The registry's grade is 'Claimed'.
events.direction: Cuts toward a bounded-gap bound; not about EH.
people: Nine credited human authors per the registry (names not verified; search summaries list Charton, Hong, Lau, Ono, Remy, Siu, Swaminathan, Thorner, Xie)

events.what_happened: Shiva Kintali announced on 1 Sep 2026 on X that he had 'showed that H1 <= 236 with the help of AI, building on Julia Stadlmann's work' (X post not opened; quoted in search results). His personal homepage (opened) lists 'Improved Bounded Gaps Between Primes. H1 <= 236', status Preprint, with a relative link to a PDF (papers/Prime-Gaps.pdf) that was not opened. The homepage quotes him: 'Building upon Julia Stadlmann's ideas, I proved H1 <= 236 using AI.' VibeMathed (opened) lists it as 'Candidate (review pending)', no named model, and 'no preprint', which conflicts with the homepage link.
events.revisions: Kintali said on 3 Sep that his record lasted two days after Axiom's 212.
events.delivers: Claims H1 ≤ 236 (bounded gaps). Not EH. The method per VibeMathed (secondhand): GPY combined with the Maynard–Tao sieve.
events.remains: EH; the paper is not available to read.
events.doubts: The paper PDF was not read. VibeMathed says the disclosure does not name the AI model or describe the division of labour, and it is unreviewed. A separate arXiv-ePrint paper claims the same bound (see next event); the relationship between the two is not stated.
events.direction: Claims a bounded-gap bound; not about EH.

events.what_happened: Zhao Song and Song Yue (Northeastern University), 'Bounded Gaps Between Primes: An Upper Bound of 236', IACR ePrint 2026/1893 (received 4 Sep 2026; approved 9 Sep 2026; ePrint landing page opened; PDF returned HTTP 403 and was not read). Abstract: proves H1 ≤ 236, building on Zhang, Maynard, Polymath (246) and Stadlmann (240). The page says nothing about AI and does not say whether EH or a level of distribution is used.
events.revisions: Received 4 Sep 2026; approved 9 Sep 2026.
events.delivers: A bounded-gap bound H1 ≤ 236. Not EH.

The entry notes a prime-number-theorem consequence with error O(x^(7/8+ε)); it states no level of distribution and no EH consequence. summary: Nothing read shows the Elliott–Halberstam conjecture itself, for every θ < 1, proved or disproved since 26 January 2024. The record has four kinds of in-window material and one pre-window claim. (a) Conditional results: Kandhil, Languasco and Moree (arXiv 2411.19762, 29 Nov 2024; Math. Ann. 394 (2026)) prove that EH holds under GRH plus a pair-correlation conjecture for Dirichlet L-functions. This is the nearest thing to a resolution, but it rests on unproven hypotheses, so it is a different-hypotheses version; Trey Smith (arXiv 2511.14810, 17 Nov 2025) proposes a generalised conjecture GEH-2 that he says implies the twin-prime conjecture; Ghadimi (arXiv 2507.17986) is heuristic under a partial EH; Cantarini (arXiv 2607.09110) and Kandhil et al. (arXiv 2607.14515) are conditional on GRH and related hypotheses. (b) Unconditional progress on variants: Pascadi (arXiv 2505.00653, 1 May 2025) gives level 5/8 − o(1) for primes in arithmetic progressions with triply well-factorable weights and says the Selberg-eigenvalue dependence of Lichtman's earlier 5/8 is removed. Li (arXiv 2505.09629, 30 Apr 2025) gives a minorant with distribution level 10/19 for smooth moduli. Neither proves the unweighted sum over all moduli q ≤ x^θ for any θ > 1/2, and both are restricted or weighted. This is the closest call in the record. (c) The bounded-gap race of Aug–Oct 2026: Stadlmann (arXiv 2608.31126, 31 Aug 2026) gives H1 ≤ 240 using smooth-modulus equidistribution estimates whose exponent the part read does not state; Song–Yue (ePrint 2026/1893) and Kintali (announced 1 Sep 2026) give H1 ≤ 236; Axiom (3 Sep 2026) gives H1 ≤ 212 with a Lean certificate; OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra gives H1 ≤ 186 (repository openai/PrimeGaps186, conditional on three Kloosterman and integral-bound axioms). These bound H1, not the level θ. The 186 result's inputs in the PDF (equidistribution estimates for triply densely divisible moduli) are secondhand, since the PDF was not readable. The judging pass must decide whether any of them moves the EH quantity; Stadlmann's abstract does not claim a level beyond 1/2. (d) OpenAI's 6 Oct 2026 zero-free-region claim for all Dirichlet L-functions: the registry entry gives PNT error O(x^(7/8+ε)), states no level of distribution, and nobody outside the lab has checked it. (e) A DeepMind formal-conjectures issue (2 Apr 2026, closed 20 Jul 2026 via PR #4459) adds a Lean statement of EH for every 0 < ϑ < 1; a statement, not a proof. Pre-window background is in the events: Bombieri–Vinogradov (θ < 1/2); Friedlander–Granville 1989 (the endpoint fails with a log-power loss); Polymath8a (1/2 + 7/300 for smooth squarefree moduli); Lichtman 2023 (weighted 66/107); Stadlmann 2023 (1/2 + 1/40 for smooth moduli); and the conditional consequence papers (Maynard 2013, Tao 2014, Debouzy 2019). Volfson's 2015 preprint claims EH 'with probability arbitrarily close to 1'. That is a probabilistic statement, not the deterministic conjecture, and no journal, review or withdrawal was found. AI: no source ties any AI system to the mathematics of EH itself. Every AI-involved event found sits in neighbouring problems: bounded gaps (OpenAI 186, Axiom 212 and 246, Kintali 236), zero-free regions (OpenAI, 6 Oct 2026), and a formal statement generated by an unnamed AI agent (the DeepMind issue). Only the OpenAI repository gives an authors' own, quotable account of AI credit, and it is a Lean-formalisation credit ('agent', 'GPT 6 Astra', 'Codex'). The Axiom 212 AI role comes from a registry paraphrase of an appendix I could not read. Other AI leads checked and found unrelated to EH: GPT-5.6 Sol's Erdős–Rankin prime-gap entry (Aug 2026, Wikipedia AI list, not opened); a Linnik/Liouville Goldbach claim attributed to GPT-6 Astra (21 Sep 2026, secondhand, not opened). Wikipedia's current EH article (not the frozen revision) states 'the lowest proven bound is 240' without a citation for the unconditional 240. This record does not use it as evidence.
competing_reading: Pascadi's weighted level 5/8 (2025), and the smooth-modulus equidistribution inputs used by the 2026 bounded-gap results, could be read as unconditional progress on the EH quantity: a level of distribution above 1/2, obtained for a class of moduli or with weights, that the conjecture asks about in part. On that reading the EH problem has moved in the window, but only in restricted or weighted form. The reading against it: the conjecture asks for the unweighted sum over all moduli q ≤ x^θ, and each of these results either restricts the moduli or the weights, or bounds a different quantity (H1). A reader could also argue that Volfson's probabilistic claim is an EH proof in the probabilistic sense, but the conjecture is deterministic, so this reading is weak.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The main theorem of Pascadi arXiv 2505.00653: is the 5/8 level for weighted sums only, or for unweighted sums too, and for which moduli? (2) The section of Stadlmann arXiv 2608.31126 that states the exponent for the smooth-modulus equidistribution, and whether it covers the unweighted sum. (3) The full text of the OpenAI 'Improved short gaps between primes' PDF and of Axiom's bgp212.pdf, Appendix A, to fix what each inputs and what AI supplied. (4) Expert reading of any of these by Maynard, Lichtman, Pascadi, Stadlmann or others in the area. (5) The IACR ePrint 2026/1893 PDF, to see whether it uses EH or a level beyond 1/2. (6) A deterministic version of Volfson's argument or a referee report on it, if one exists.

judgement.why: The statement is EH for every θ < 1 on the unweighted sum over all moduli. Bombieri–Vinogradov settles the range θ < 1/2, a pre-snapshot case. Every post-snapshot event changes the question: Kandhil–Languasco–Moree prove EH only under GRH plus pair correlation (variant, not a case, because the extra hypotheses alter the question rather than restrict its range); Pascadi 5/8 and Lichtman use triply well-factorable weights, and Polymath8a, Stadlmann and Li restrict to smooth moduli or a minorant, so they bound a different sum (variant, not bound). The close call was whether restricted-moduli levels count as a 'case' (a class of objects); I judged them variants because they bound a different sum rather than proving EH's full bound for a subclass at every θ < 1. The bounded-gap results concern H1, a different quantity. Friedlander–Granville refutes only the endpoint, which lies outside the statement's range. The only AI quote (PrimeGaps186) describes formalisation and proof checking, so its role is none, and that event is a variant anyway.
judgement.doubts: Pascadi 2505.00653's main theorem was not read; if it gave an unweighted level 5/8 over all moduli, it would be a bound on EH's quantity rather than a variant. The record suggests it does not. The claim that GPT-6 found factorisation conditions is secondhand and does not affect this problem.
